On your break / Site planning

Which meal service fits your shift pattern?

A busy lunchtime canteen can still leave the night shift with few options. When choosing food provision for several shifts, start by following one person through a real break.

Time the entire round trip

Start at the workstation. How long does someone need to reach a hot meal and get back? Include changing clothes, crossing the site and queuing. Consider a thirty-minute break. If walking takes twelve minutes in total and ordering and payment take six, only twelve minutes remain to eat. Placing the service beside the break room changes that calculation.

Look at one week, shift by shift

Record who is on site, when each group can eat and what is open at that hour. An office of a hundred people with staggered office days has a different pattern from a warehouse with the same fifty people on site every evening. Ask colleagues on Sundays and late shifts directly. A lunchtime survey can easily miss them.

Match the service to the gap

Where large teams take lunch together, a canteen counter can serve several people in parallel. Teams with fixed meal times can trial pre-ordering. When breaks are staggered and the kitchen closes early, a meal machine is another option. A LECKERDING machine can heat a selected dish inside the machine, or dispense the same meal chilled for later.

Check access and servicing

Walk the proposed spot with facilities and shift management. Can every shift enter the area? Can the service team reach it for restocking? Will the machine fit through the narrowest doorway? For an initial assessment in Berlin or Brandenburg, a photo, the access measurements and the address give us a good starting point.

Agree what the trial should answer

Choose two or three questions before starting. Can colleagues on late shifts find a suitable meal? Do they have enough time to eat? Which dishes do they miss? Agree who will collect comments and compare that feedback with actual demand. That gives the team a basis for deciding whether to continue.
